scores.evidence: M1 (In: ... cited streaming answers; Out: handoff, threshold tuning, abuse controls beyond basic limits)
scores.rationale: Mostly substrate→up (ingest→retrieval→eval→safety→pilot), but the M1 slice generates answers before the threshold, defenses and handoff are proven.

scores.evidence: Widget on a staging page streaming answers with citations... Pipeline deploys staging from `main`
scores.rationale: M1 is a real end-to-end slice with CI and IaC, but it runs in staging, not production; production first appears in M3.

scores.evidence: D0 Build ... Revisit if: The vendor bot passes our eval set ... and expected resolutions × price is below about 1.5× the build-and-run cost
scores.rationale: Assumptions A1–A9 and decisions D0–D10 give defaults, reversibility and explicit revisit triggers, with spikes stating what would change the plan.

scores.evidence: T1 scaffold → T2 infra/T3 migration → T6 connector; Gateway T4; visibility gate in M1
scores.rationale: Shared substrate (schema, gateway, visibility) comes before leaf work, but the plan never frames ordering by blast radius, and some wide items like abuse controls are pushed to M2.

scores.evidence: Security (M1 for the basics, M2 for hardening)
scores.rationale: M1 has the visibility gate, XSS protection, redaction and secrets, but injection defenses, abuse controls and retention sit in M2, and the treatment is a standalone section rather than per-phase.

scores.evidence: T15 Add basic telemetry: OpenTelemetry traces with per-stage spans, JSON logs with conversation_id, metrics for TTFT, errors and cost
scores.rationale: Telemetry is in M1, dashboards and alerts arrive in M2, and cost dashboards and A/B measurement continue in M3 and M4.

scores.evidence: `terraform apply` from CI creates the environment; ... image tagged with the commit SHA; prompts and config in version control; eval datasets in git
scores.rationale: IaC, pinned image SHAs, versioned index, config hash, migrations and versioned eval sets make builds and data reproducible from M1 onward.

scores.evidence: Gateway: timeouts, one retry, fallback model; per-article transactions, cursor advances only on success; degraded mode; M2 injected provider failure
scores.rationale: Failure handling appears in M1 (gateway, idempotent ingestion), M2 (degraded modes, handoff idempotency, restore test), and M3–M4 (flags, rollback).

scores.evidence: M1 Out: handoff, threshold tuning, abuse controls beyond basic limits; M2 adds 'No-answer threshold and sentinel'
scores.rationale: Human-in-the-loop handoff, budgets and injection defenses come in M2, after the M1 generation and retrieval are built; the retrieval→model→feedback order is right, but defenses are not before capabilities.

scores.evidence: Account-specific answers ... Trigger to build: Q3 is 'yes' and the ticket mix shows more than 20% are account lookups.
scores.rationale: A deferred-work table gives a concrete pull-forward trigger for each item, plus named debt reviewed at M4.

note: A strong, detailed plan with excellent tradeoff gates, deferrals, observability and resilience. It is weakened by a staging-only first slice and by AI defenses and handoff landing in M2, after the M1 generation path.
